C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY.Summary: Close the recorded engine-parity debt of the search zone: one documented semantic table governs both search engines (the embedded ignore/regex walker and the rg shell-out) across all four transport legs (content walker, files walker, content rg search, rg files listing), one shared flag-resolution source feeds every leg so the same options and the same fixture cannot produce different result sets depending on which engine a machine selected, the case mode becomes explicit-option-only on both engines (the pattern-dependent --smart-case implicit mode is removed as the divergence source), .gitignore handling outside a git repository becomes identical on both engines (the rg transports gain --no-require-git, making the walker leg's long-standing comment true), the walker's byte-offset snippet truncation stops panicking on multi-byte content (the recorded triple-debt entry (the UTF-8 truncation item named verbatim in the NonGoals of C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY, C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD and C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE)) and is pinned by a failing-first Cyrillic/emoji regression test, and a parameterized parity suite runs one fixture through both engines with identical expectations for case modes, gitignore outside git, hidden files and exclusion masks.
C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY.Problem: Confirmed against the fork/main state of src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs (VERSION 2.6.0-beta, C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE merged); line anchors below are from that state. The zone runs TWO engines selected per machine in mt_search_spawn: App Store builds always take the in-process walker and desktop builds take system rg unless the binary is missing (:990-999, the BLOCK_RIPGREP_FALLBACK marker at :996), so a divergence between the legs is invisible on one machine and flips behavior between machines. Four divergences are live. (1) Case mode: the walker's build_matcher compiles the pattern with case_insensitive(!opts.is_case_sensitive.unwrap_or(false)) (:671-673) — with the default options it matches case-INsensitively regardless of the pattern's letter case; the rg content transport passes --case-sensitive when the option is true and --smart-case otherwise (:1115-1119) — and rg's documented smart-case mode searches case-sensitively whenever the pattern contains any uppercase character, so the pattern "Needle" with default options returns "needle", "NEEDLE" and "Needle" on the walker leg but only "Needle" on the rg leg. The renderer's explicit isCaseSensitive toggle (tests/renderer/store/search.test.ts "toggles isCaseSensitive flag") is silently overridden by the pattern text on the rg leg only. (2) Gitignore outside a git repository: both walker legs honor .gitignore everywhere — run_files_walker :576 and the content walker :834 call require_git(false) with the comment "(matches ripgrep --no-require-git)" — but neither rg transport passes that flag: START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_COMMAND (:1109-1145) and START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_FILES_COMMAND (:1413-1446) contain no --no-require-git, and rg's default requires a git repository before consulting gitignore sources. In a plain (non-git) folder the same fixture is filtered on the walker leg and unfiltered on the rg leg; the walker comment claims a parity that was never delivered. (3) UTF-8 truncation panic (the recorded triple-debt entry (the UTF-8 truncation item named verbatim in the NonGoals of C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY, C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD and C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE)): the content walker byte-slices the line at the 1 MB cap — "let truncated = line.len() > MAX_LINE_BYTES;" and "format!(\"{}…\", &line[..MAX_LINE_BYTES.min(line.len())])" (:892-897, MAX_LINE_BYTES = 1024 * 1024 at :91) — and a Rust byte-slice panics when the cap offset lands inside a multi-byte character (Cyrillic letters are 2 bytes, emoji 4), so a line of Cyrillic or emoji text long enough to cross the cap crashes the walker leg's search thread; the leg is the only engine on App Store builds and the fallback on rg-less desktops. The boundary-safe helper byte_offset_to_utf16_units (:154) cannot help — the panic happens at snippet construction, before bounds conversion. The only truncation test, match_beyond_truncated_snippet_yields_absent_bounds (:3414), builds its fixture from ASCII ("x".repeat(MAX_LINE_BYTES + 10), :3421), so the multi-byte panic is unpinned. (4) The files-mode per-transport size divergence this change already owns: the files walker leg applies max_file_size as a metadata skip (:578-580) while the rg --files listing transport passes no --max-filesize by an explicit recorded decision (:1414-1419: "this per-transport size divergence is documented in the plan and owned by C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY"; the archive Assumption of C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE repeats the assignment) — the note is still open on the delivery baseline. Rows that already agree and must stay agreeing: hidden files (walker .hidden :571/:829, rg --hidden only on include_hidden :1123-1125), the ignore-family switches (walker .ignore/.git_ignore/.git_global/.git_exclude from one respect_ignore value :568/:572-575 and :826-833, rg --no-ignore on the same option :1126-1128, otherwise rg defaults), exclusion masks (one compile_exclusion_masks :703 feeding walker overrides :846-858 and rg --glob=! arguments :1136-1139), content-mode maxFileSize (:836-838 versus --max-filesize :1140-1142), follow_symlinks (:835 versus --follow :1129-1131), whole-word and literal/regex handling (:661-670 versus --fixed-strings :1112-1114 and --word-regexp :1120-1122). The legacy per-leg column values remain a recorded debt superseded for rendering by the #320 bounds (walker hit-emission comment :905-912) and stay out of scope.

Goals.Goal: One parity table, one flag source. The engine semantics of the search zone are documented exactly once — a single parity table in the change record covering every option and ignore-source row (case mode, hidden, .ignore, .gitignore inside and outside git, git-global excludes, git-info excludes, no_ignore, exclusion masks, inclusions, maxFileSize per mode, follow_symlinks, whole-word, literal/regex) with the agreed semantic and the owning code anchor per engine leg — and one shared flag-resolution artifact (a single function or struct consumed by both walker builders and both rg command builders) is the only place where engine flags are chosen, so a future option cannot reach one leg and not the other. The BUILD_RIPGREP_COMMAND and BUILD_RIPGREP_FILES_COMMAND blocks and the two WalkBuilder chains all draw from that one source; per-leg leftovers are only the legs' inherent shape (rg process arguments versus ignore-crate builder calls) and the documented files-mode size row.

Explicit-option-only case mode on both engines: the renderer's isCaseSensitive toggle is the only case control. With the toggle off, both engines match case-insensitively for every pattern, including Mixed-case patterns; with the toggle on, both match exactly. The pattern-dependent implicit smart-case mode is removed from the rg leg's argument set (the --smart-case branch at :1115-1119 is replaced by the explicit insensitive default), the walker's existing semantics (:671-673) become the canon unchanged, and the parity table documents the removal. No renderer change: the toggle, its store wiring and its tests stay as they are.

Identical gitignore semantics inside and outside git repositories: the walker's documented require_git(false) behavior becomes the canon on both engines, and both rg transports (content :1109-1145 and files listing :1413-1446) pass --no-require-git through the shared flag source, making the walker legs' "(matches ripgrep --no-require-git)" comments (:576, :834) true. The .ignore-file semantics are unaffected (rg honors .ignore regardless of git presence, matching the walker's .ignore switch), and the no_ignore option keeps disabling all ignore sources on both engines.

Boundary-safe snippet truncation (closes the recorded triple-debt entry (the UTF-8 truncation item named verbatim in the NonGoals of C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY, C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD and C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE)): the content walker truncates at MAX_LINE_BYTES without panic by flooring to the last UTF-8 character boundary at or before the cap, delivers the same ellipsis marker, truncated flag and honest-or-absent bounds as today, and keeps the cap value unchanged (the V-M-004 "no full-line buffer over 4 MB" budget holds). A failing-first regression test with a Cyrillic/emoji fixture crossing the cap byte proves no panic and honest delivery; the existing ASCII truncation pin (:3414) stays green.

A parameterized parity suite proves the table: one fixture set, both engines, identical expectations per row — case modes (default and toggle-on, including a Mixed-case pattern), gitignore outside a git repository (content mode and files mode), hidden files and exclusion masks — with the rg legs under the existing availability guard (the rg_available precedent, :2160/:3324). The files-mode size row is resolved in the table as documented engine-inherent divergence: the walker metadata skip (:578-580) is the canon, the rg --files listing is recorded as not size-filtered, the comment at :1414-1419 is updated to point at the delivered table row, and the safety argument (quickOpen never sends maxFileSize in files mode) is recorded with it.

Constraints.Constraint: Engine selection and session machinery are unchanged: the App Store in-process decision, the missing-rg fallback with BLOCK_RIPGREP_FALLBACK (:990-999), the files-mode discriminator dispatch (START_BLOCK_FILES_MODE_DISPATCH :1022-1035), the 120 ms warm-up, the registry insert/remove lifecycle, SearchSessionCoordinator's seq and single-terminal ownership, M-010 root validation and the mt::search-event envelope (kinds match/complete/cancelled/error, additive optional partial, additive optional matchStart/matchEnd) are not edited. No new rg flag beyond --no-require-git and the case-mode replacement argument; no new wire field; no new event kind or channel.

The case-mode canon is the walker's explicit-option semantics: build_matcher keeps case_insensitive(!opts.is_case_sensitive.unwrap_or(false)) unchanged (:671-673) and the existing walker case suites stay green verbatim (case_insensitive_default :1779, case_sensitive_excludes_mismatched_case :1793); the rg leg's change is confined to the case branch of the shared flag source (--ignore-case explicit option instead of --smart-case), and the parity table records that smart-case's implicit pattern-dependence was the divergence source. bounds_parity_across_engines (:3324) keeps passing — its fixture uses a lowercase pattern, whose behavior is identical before and after.

The gitignore-outside canon is the walker's require_git(false) (:576, :834): the fix adds --no-require-git to both rg transports via the shared flag source and does not touch any walker line. The existing walker ignore suites stay green verbatim (gitignore_excluded_files_skipped :1821, no_ignore_includes_gitignored_files :1834, hidden_files_skipped_by_default :1983, include_hidden_picks_up_dotfiles :1995, exclusions_applied_symmetrically :2485, invalid_exclusion_mask_is_ignored_and_forces_partial :2559, rg_exit_two_is_single_error_terminal :2314); inside a git repository no behavior changes on either engine.

Truncation safety is local to the snippet construction site (:892-897): the byte cap value MAX_LINE_BYTES (:91), the ellipsis marker, the truncated flag, delivered_end_byte and the honest-or-absent bounds rule (:898-912 region) keep their contracts; only the slicing becomes boundary-safe (floor to the last char boundary at or before the cap — the cap only shrinks the delivered text by at most three bytes, never grows it). byte_offset_to_utf16_units (:154) is not edited. The files-mode path-only legs stay body-read-free (the START_BLOCK_WALKER_PATH_LEG contract, :550-556) — truncation does not apply to them.

The files-mode size row is documentation-plus-comment only: no flag is added to the rg --files listing (the listing transport must not gain --max-filesize on this change's authority), the walker metadata skip stays as canon, and the updated comment at the START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_FILES_COMMAND block points at the parity table row with the quickOpen-never-sends-maxFileSize safety argument inherited from the #333 record.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No unification of the two engines into one implementation: rg shell-out and the embedded walker both stay, with identical documented semantics — this change aligns behavior and flag sourcing, not architecture. No rg sidecar bundling (B4), no search ranking, no context-line delivery, no regex-syntax changes, no new search features, no result-order guarantees beyond the existing ordinary traversal order.

No renderer work of any kind: no store, component, shim, locale or typed-facade edit; #320's matchStart/matchEnd contract, #324's generation and delivered-match cap semantics (SEARCH_RESULT_CAP = 100) and #333's FILES_RESULT_CAP = 30 and path-only hit shape are consumed as-is. The legacy per-leg column values stay the recorded superseded debt (#320 bounds supersede them for rendering; walker comment :905-912) — no column unification here.

No tree-emit batching, no walker result-delivery cost work and no files-mode cost redesign beyond the one documented size-table row: the traversal-cost items #324/#333 recorded as this bundle's territory are consciously left open here and stay recorded as debt — the parity suite pins semantics, not throughput. No changes to FILES_RESULT_CAP, cap honesty, partial-flag computation or terminal behavior.

No dependency acquisition, no Cargo.toml or feature changes, no release version, tags or publication; no preferences schema change (the isCaseSensitive option keeps its name, wire shape and default on both engines).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first parity test, case modes: one fixture containing "needle", "NEEDLE" and "Needle" lines searched with default options yields the same result set on the walker leg and the rg leg (availability-guarded) — all three case variants, proving the Mixed-case pattern no longer toggles sensitivity implicitly; the same fixture with isCaseSensitive true yields only the exact line on both legs; a lowercase-pattern case repeats the #320 parity shape. Today the rg leg returns one variant while the walker returns three, so the test is red before the fix; case_insensitive_default and case_sensitive_excludes_mismatched_case stay green.

Failing-first parity test, gitignore outside git: a TempDir fixture (no .git) with a .gitignore listing one file and a sibling file both containing the needle is searched by both engines in content mode and both legs in files mode — the gitignored file is absent and the sibling present on every leg, identically. Today the walker legs filter and the rg legs do not, so the test is red before the fix; gitignore_excluded_files_skipped and no_ignore_includes_gitignored_files stay green; a companion assertion records that inside a git-repository fixture nothing changes.

Failing-first UTF-8 regression pin (F-007): a walker-leg line whose byte length exceeds MAX_LINE_BYTES and whose multi-byte characters straddle the cap offset (Cyrillic and emoji in the fixture) is searched without panic; the hit is delivered with truncated true, the ellipsis marker, and honest-or-absent bounds per the #320 rule; the delivered snippet is valid UTF-8 and no longer than the current cap plus the marker. Today the byte slice at :894 panics on this fixture, so the test is red (panics) before the fix; match_beyond_truncated_snippet_yields_absent_bounds (:3414) stays green with its ASCII fixture.

Parity-table regression pins for the agreeing rows: hidden files (default skip and include_hidden) and exclusion masks (masked file absent, sibling present, invalid mask ignored with the partial flag) are asserted identically on both legs by the parameterized suite, keeping hidden_files_skipped_by_default, include_hidden_picks_up_dotfiles, exclusions_applied_symmetrically and invalid_exclusion_mask_is_ignored_and_forces_partial green; the files-mode size row is present in the parity table with the walker-canon decision and the updated pointer comment at the files-command block.

One flag source is provable: both rg transports and both walker chains consume the shared flag-resolution artifact — a test or structural assertion demonstrates that the case and gitignore decisions are made in exactly one place (for example, the parity fixtures above fail loudly if one leg is edited without the other, and the file-local contract names the artifact as the single flag authority); MODULE_MAP and CHANGE_SUMMARY describe it; no per-leg hardcoded flag for the aligned rows remains outside it.

Neighbor-wave pins stay green without weakened assertions or budgets: the #320 family (search_hit_bounds_wire_form :3283, bounds_parity_across_engines :3324, match_beyond_truncated_snippet_yields_absent_bounds :3414, rg_bounds_absent_when_submatch_exceeds_delivered_line :3447), the #333 family (files_mode_walker_lists_paths_without_reading_bodies :3620, files_mode_inclusions_filter_both_legs :3718, files_mode_cap_truncates_and_marks_partial :3843, files_mode_rg_transport_honesty :3942, files_mode_rg_parity_with_walker_on_one_fixture :4108, files_mode_mid_walk_cancel_drains_pending_batch_then_single_terminal :4188), the #303 honesty family (rg_exit_two_is_single_error_terminal :2314, rg_exit_codes_zero_and_one_complete_normally), and the renderer #324 pins in tests/renderer/store/search.test.ts ("a stale generation completing while the newest runs leaves running true" :408, "a stale generation completing after the newest cannot overwrite its results" :438, "caps the displayed set at 100 delivered matches and marks it partial" :239) all pass; graph ownership and verification (M-004 SummaryDelta, V-M-004 entry) describe the final implementation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Named new tests pin the behaviors: engine_parity_case_modes_across_legs (Mixed-case default and toggle-on identical on both legs), engine_parity_gitignore_outside_git_across_legs (content and files modes, no-git fixture, walker-canon filtering on every leg), walker_utf8_boundary_truncation_does_not_panic (Cyrillic/emoji cap-crossing fixture, honest delivery, red before the fix), engine_parity_hidden_and_excludes_across_legs (agreeing rows pinned green). The failing-first three are recorded red on the pre-change baseline (case and gitignore as result-set mismatches, truncation as a panic) with receipts preserved as pre-change evidence, not relabeled. Existing receipts — the #289 session-trace family, the #303 honesty family, the #320 bounds family and the #333 files-mode family — are preserved as pre-change evidence. The rg legs run under the existing availability guard; unavailable-platform or owner acceptance evidence remains explicitly open and is not substituted by a shim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The rg flag contract is treated as the documented rg behavior: --smart-case searches case-insensitively only when the pattern is all-lowercase; the default (no --no-require-git) consults gitignore sources only inside a git repository; --no-require-git lifts exactly that gate without touching .ignore handling. The plan verifies all three once against the delivery baseline's rg version before pinning tests, as #303 did for the exit-code contract.

The case-mode direction is deliberate: explicit-option-only semantics (toggle off means case-insensitive everywhere) are chosen over promoting smart-case to both engines because the renderer already exposes an explicit case toggle, an implicit pattern-dependent override of an explicit control made the two engines disagree and made results depend on the query's letter case on one engine only, and the walker's semantics are the tested status quo the renderer suites already pin. If the plan documents a different single semantic with equivalent parity, the acceptance criterion is the identical-across-legs contract, not the specific direction.

The files-mode size row resolves as documentation (walker metadata skip is canon; the rg --files listing is recorded as not size-filtered; quickOpen never sends maxFileSize in files mode) because the listing transport must not gain content-search-time filters on this change's authority; if the plan verifies on the delivery baseline that rg --files honors --max-filesize and documents adding it, the parity-table row must state the delivered truth either way — the acceptance criterion is one documented row, not a specific flag.

The UTF-8 fix keeps MAX_LINE_BYTES as a byte cap (the V-M-004 budget is stated in bytes) and accepts the at-most-three-byte shrinkage at the boundary; a character-count cap would change the budget unit and is out of scope.
Approval of this specification does not approve an unwritten plan, apply/archive, lane departure or release.
